- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought signals.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.7 to 0.1) and price is rising, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 3 days.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative (0.3–0.6) and recent price is trending down; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid “mean reversion trap”.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 10-day average unless sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overestimates; apply 1–2% downward correction to avoid “sentiment-driven overreach”.
